raw_posts.title: Mon Aug 24 – Whale Watching
raw_posts.content: Today we sailed southeast to find cetaceans in an area where several humpbacks have been seen previously. On the way, we found two large groups of Tamanend’s bottlenose dolphins (at least 120-150 individuals each) which we shared an exceptional encounter with. Typically, Tamanend’s are relatively shy around our vessels and disappear beneath the surface when moving near us. These dolphins, however, remained adjacent to the Viking Star, porpoising, interacting, and circle feeding providing incredible views into this species’ daily lives. We continued south and came across an ocean sunfish, Mola mola, which was resting at the surface. The densest of all bony fish, this animal did not mind our presence and moved under the vessel from one side to the other, allowing everyone to observe this unique species! raw_posts.content: Despite a light drizzle at the dock, we sailed away from Montauk under cloudy, but dry conditions, and found our first whale approximately three miles from shore. This was a minke whale, the smallest of baleen whales, which surfaced regularly around the vessel in short (30 seconds to 1.5 minutes) intervals while feeding on the rich abundance of bait (likely silversides) at the surface. Minkes are generally fast and elusive, so it was a treat to observe this cetacean within a small area with repeated, multiple views. We moved on and a few miles later encountered numerous pods of Tamanend’s bottlenose dolphin. raw_posts.title: Wed August 12 – Whale Watching
raw_posts.content: Humpback moms and calves in action! Under clear skies and cool ocean breezes, the Viking Starship headed east in search of the whales that have been in the region all summer, but have recently spread out as bait has also been on the move. We passed beautiful Block Island on calm seas before investigating a spout a few miles from the island. all_videos.title: He Invented the Albie Snax. His New Lure Is an 11-Inch Freak.
all_videos.description:
Alex Peru grew up in Fairfield, CT turning wooden plugs and chasing false albacore — and when nothing on the market matched what he saw on the water, he built his own. The result was the Albie Snax: a 5-inch, half-ounce soft plastic that casts like a bullet and catches everything from albies to striped bass. We sell about a thousand a year in white alone.

In this conversation, Alex breaks down the actual engineering: why stiffness beats weight for casting distance, why the Albie Snax is cylindrical (and what a cupcake has to do with it), the rigging tricks most anglers never try, and the surprising fact that the Super Snax came first.

all_videos.title: Fishing Teasers and Baits for Blue Marlin with Mike Hennessy | In The Spread
all_videos.description:
Blue marlin edge fishing with Captain Mike Hennessy. Bait and switch tactics around offshore seamounts and structure, and how to convert a teaser-raised fish into a hookup.

Blue marlin do not scatter randomly across open water. They set up on structure. Seamounts, drop-offs, and current breaks concentrate bait, and that is where marlin hunt from ambush. Fish those edges with a plan and you are hunting predictable zones instead of dragging baits and hoping to cross paths with a fish.

In this trailer, Captain Mike Hennessy draws on decades of edge fishing to break down the bait and switch: teasers pull fish in without hooks, then a well-placed ballyhoo or skipjack seals the deal once the marlin commits.

all_videos.title: Teasers for Blue Marlin Fishing with Mike Hennessy
all_videos.description:
Blue marlin teaser fishing with Captain Mike Hennessy. Learn how teasers create visual commotion that pulls fish in from beyond lure range and converts curious marlin into hookups.

Teasers do not carry hooks. They create chaos. The disturbance mimics a baitfish school under attack, and that is exactly what a blue marlin instinctively swims over to investigate. Get the commotion right and you pull fish into your spread from well beyond the range where lures alone get noticed. Get it wrong and you are just dragging plastic and hoping.
